questions.q: Why isn't a single group-membership query enough to answer 'who has access to the OT/SCADA boundary'?
options: Group membership queries are too slow to run in production

Hartwell's break-glass procedure has, in the past, granted a handful of accounts direct, individually-assigned access that bypasses the groups entirely, so a group-only query would never see those accounts
Microsoft Graph does not support querying group membership
AWS IAM groups don't exist as a concept
questions.explain: Break-glass access can be granted directly to a user, never added to the group — a script that only checks group membership would never surface those accounts at all.

questions.q: What does the AWS call list_entities_for_policy with EntityFilter="User" specifically return?
options: Every IAM user in the account, regardless of policy
Exactly the users a given policy is attached to directly, not including users who only have it through group membership
Only users who have never logged in
The full text of the policy document itself
questions.explain: This call returns direct attachments only — it must run as a separate query from get_group, because it does not include access inherited through group membership.

questions.q: In the output schema this script produces, what does the access_path field distinguish?
options: Which cloud region the account is in
Whether an account's access came through group membership or was granted directly to that individual account
Whether the account is a human or a service account
The account's password complexity score
questions.explain: access_path is set to either "group_membership" or "direct_assignment", and this single field is what later lets anyone distinguish accounts a group-only review would catch from ones it would miss.

questions.q: What does the script compute as count_direct_assignment_only, and why does it matter most to later lessons?
options: The total number of AWS accounts Hartwell owns
The count of accounts whose SCADA access exists only through direct assignment, not group membership — exactly the population a group-only review would never see
The number of accounts that have been formally reviewed and approved
A count of failed login attempts against the SCADA gateway
questions.explain: count_direct_assignment_only isolates accounts with standing access granted outside any group — the exact gap a group-membership-only methodology misses, which is the mechanism this capstone's later discrepancy depends on.

questions.q: Where do the normalized inventory records get written, and why does that matter?
options: Only to a local CSV file on Mara's laptop, with no further use
Into a Log Analytics custom table named ScadaAccessInventory_CL via the Logs Ingestion API, making it queryable from Microsoft Sentinel rather than a one-off script output
Directly into the Entra ID directory as a new attribute
Into an email sent to the whole IT department
questions.explain: Writing into the ScadaAccessInventory_CL custom log table through the Logs Ingestion API is what makes this a SIEM-based inventory — any Sentinel analyst can query current standing access with KQL instead of re-running the script's raw output.
